dateline: Hawthorne, CA / Boca Chica, TX — May 2002–Present
heroHeadline: Starlink 10-53 Completes 617th Booster Recovery — 66th 2026 Mission; FAA IFT-12 Investigation Rationale Detailed; IPO Roadshow 6 Days Away
heroSubtitle: 8,788 days since SpaceX founding — Falcon 9 booster B1085 (16th flight) launched 29 Starlink V2 Mini satellites from SLC-40 Cape Canaveral at 12:57 UTC, landing on 'A Shortfall of Gravitas' for the 617th cumulative SpaceX booster recovery (ASOG's 152nd touchdown). The FAA mishap investigation rationale for the IFT-12 Booster 19 anomaly was detailed in a May 29 explainer: mandatory review triggered under 14 CFR Part 401 after multiple outer ring Raptor 3 engines failed to ignite during the boostback burn, causing uncontrolled booster descent. IFT-13 (Booster 20 + Ship 40) remains on target for July–August 2026 pending FAA review resolution (expected late June). The IPO management roadshow begins in 6 days (June 4–8), with pricing June 11 and Nasdaq (SPCX) debut June 12 targeting a $75–80B raise at $1.75–2T implied valuation. Starlink constellation: 10,510+ active satellites, 10.3M subscribers.
